topic: What happens in the 1 second after you send a WhatsApp message?
title: What Happens the Second You Hit Send on WhatsApp 💬
description: Before your message leaves your phone, it's locked with end-to-end encryption that only your friend's phone can open.
It hops through cell towers, fiber and WhatsApp's servers — which only ever see scrambled noise.
sources: WhatsApp – Encryption Overview, technical white paper (Signal Protocol; WhatsApp has no plaintext access): https://www.whatsapp.com/security/WhatsApp-Security-Whitepaper.pdf

TechCrunch – WhatsApp is now delivering roughly 100 billion messages a day; over 2 billion users (Oct 2020): https://techcrunch.com/2020/10/29/whatsapp-is-now-delivering-roughly-100-billion-messages-a-day/
Panda Security – WhatsApp check marks explained (one grey, two grey, two blue): https://www.pandasecurity.com/en/mediacenter/whatsapp-check-marks/

beats.narration: Your WhatsApp message is *locked* before it even leaves your phone.
It's called end-to-end encryption: your phone locks it with a key only your friend's phone has.
Then, in a fraction of a second, it hops to a cell tower, races through fiber cables, and reaches WhatsApp's servers.
But those servers only ever see *scrambled noise*. Not even WhatsApp itself can read what you wrote.
One grey tick: the server has it. Two ticks: it reached their phone. Blue: they *read* it.
And WhatsApp does this about *100 billion* times a day, for over two billion people.
